title: Onboarding: data handoff & ephemeral ops notes
content:
Context and goal:
- Working notes from pre-onboarding workshop for a regulated customer (industry: digital therapeutics).
- Outcome: agree minimal retention path so POC telemetry + user prompts are safe for demo and field trial. Prepare DPA addendum language for minimal-storage experiment.

High-level proposal (single-paragraph):
- For POC phase we propose ephemeral session-first architecture: all session-level request/response KV entries are kept in in-memory TTL caches (KV-cache) on serving nodes and only flushed to durable storage when explicitly requested by customer for debugging (opt-in). Default TTL: 30 minutes; configurable per-customer policy. Audit logs and metrics are emitted to an isolated telemetry pipeline with pseudonymized IDs, and raw prompt text is never persisted to long-term blob storage in hosted mode.

Data flow diagram (textual):
- Client -> Redwood gateway (region-sticky) -> Router policy (POC-tier route) -> Serving runtime
  - Serving runtime: prefix/KV cached per-session (in-memory: TTL 30m, eviction last-access)
  - If debug flag set: scrubbed copy -> short-term S3 bucket (30 day retention, restricted bucket, customer KMS)
  - Telemetry pipeline: token counts, latency, error codes -> metrics DB (no prompt text)
  - Audit trail: operation records (who called what, model version) -> audit log (7y retention, access-controlled)

Recommended POC settings (ops knobs):
- Default session TTL: 30 minutes (can set 0 for strict no-persist)
- Debug dump bucket TTL: 30 days (auto-expire lifecycle rule)
- Model variant for POC: quantized v1.9 (lower leak risk, lower tokenization detail)
- KMS: customer-managed key for any persisted artifacts
- IP allowlist + mutual TLS for admin endpoints

DPA addendum talking points (language sketches to hand to legal):
- "Redwood will not persist end-user prompt or model output beyond the configured session TTL unless explicitly requested in writing by the Customer for debugging or audit purposes."
- "When Customer requests persistence for debugging, persisted artifacts will be encrypted with the Customer-managed KMS, stored in a dedicated bucket with a lifecycle of no more than 30 days, and access will be limited to named Redwood engineers under two-person approval."
- "Redwood will provide audit logs that show all access to any persisted artifacts and will surface a retention report monthly to the Customer."

Privacy engineering checklist (operational):
- [ ] Default: redact email/SSNs/names heuristics at ingress (run fast regexp + ML filter).
- [ ] Add client-side scrubbing guidance for PII before sending to demo environment (provide example SDK wrapper).
- [ ] Enable prefix/KV caching but disable durable checkpointing for POC by default.
- [ ] Turn on rotation for ephemeral keys every 24 hours for dev nodes.
- [ ] Ensure telemetry pipeline buffers are stripped of raw tokens (double-check instrumentation).

Workshop action items (who/when):
- Marco: prepare SDK wrapper example that strips PHI and demo script (due 2025-11-10).
- Priya: draft DPA addendum text using the language sketches and send to Legal for preliminary review (jira/LEGAL-78) (due 2025-11-13).
- Jordan: stand up short-term debug bucket and lifecycle policy in test account; verify KMS CMK workflow (due 2025-11-17).
- Avery: build pilot routing policy (POC-tier route) and deploy to staging with TTL knobs (due 2025-11-12).

Open questions / risk knobs (needs legal/infra signoff):
- Q1: Audit log retention: product wants 7y for compliance; customer may request shorter window for POC. Do we allow per-customer audit retention sweeps? (legal input required).
- Q2: If customer requests transcript persistence for feature evaluation, do we permit pseudonymization vs full encryption? Which is acceptable to their regulator?
- Q3: Are there any export control restrictions on model weights used in Private deployment for this customer? (eng & compliance check).

Minimal persistence scenarios (tradeoffs):
- No persistence: safest privacy posture, hard to debug model failures. Good for live demos.
- Short persistence (30d): allows post-mortem + limited evals; needs KMS & access controls.
- Full persistence (customer-managed long-term): needed only when customer requests dataset building; must be under separate contract.

Example access policy (ops):
- Access groups: se-poc-admin, se-debug, legal-audit.
- se-debug can request artifacts, but a 2-approver step is enforced via ticket (Jira SE-4875).
- All accesses are logged and pushed to the audit bucket; Customer can request monthly extracts.

Notes for Private deployments / on-prem variant:
- Recommend defaulting to "no-durable-store" for demo VM images.
- Provide an offline scrubber script to run before handing back any VM or disk images.
- If customer insists on local persistence, require a signed security posture checklist and acceptance of obligations (add to SOW).

Attachment ideas for customer deliverable:
- One-page: "POC data handling summary" (graphic + bullets)
- Appendix: sample DPA addendum text + example legal clauses (redaction + debug persistence)
- Technical appendix: SDK wrapper, scrubber script, lifecycle example for S3 + KMS commands

Quick wins to reduce risk during demo:
- Turn on redaction heuristics in SDK wrapper and include a toggle in the demo UI.
- Use a dedicated POC model variant to avoid bleed from production models.
- Add explicit user-facing banner: "Do not enter PHI in demo inputs" and enforce client-side gating.

Historical notes / similar pilots:
- 2024-10 pilot with a fintech customer used a 14-day debug bucket and client-side redaction; internal post-mortem showed a missed email regex. Use both regex + ML filter.

Next meeting: 2025-11-09 10:00 PT (pre-legal sync)
Agenda: finalize opt-in flow for debug persistence, agree TTL defaults, confirm KMS ownership model.

Unresolved: allocate a product owner to track DPA sign-off process and ensure SOW amendments are issued before any durable persistence is enabled.

-- end of notes --
